6	# AI Pipeline Offloading
7	
8	Route work to the smallest useful lane. Local first. Browser second. Cloud when needed.

11	
12	| Lane | Binary | Use Case | Status |

24	## Routing Decision Tree
25	
26	```
27	Task arrives
28	├── Shell/deterministic work? → Bash tool directly (no offload)
29	├── Reasoning / code analysis? → @deepseek
30	├── General / summarization? → @qwen
31	├── Formatting / output synthesis? → @gpt-oss
32	├── Browser interaction needed? → @comet

35	└── Frontier reasoning / wide context? → @claude (main session)
36	```
37	
38	## Capacity (M2 Pro, 16GB unified memory)
39	
40	⚠️ **ONE LOCAL LLM AT A TIME. Parallel Ollama = OOM crash.**
41	
42	```
43	RAM cap:        10GB max for Ollama (out of 16GB unified)
44	Local model:    1 at a time — kill previous before loading next
45	Browser tasks:  2–3 tabs OK alongside ONE active model
46	Claude agents:  parallel OK (cloud, not local memory)
47	─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
48	Safe:    1 local model + browser tasks
49	DANGER:  2+ local models simultaneously → system crash
50	```
51	
52	Kill between models: `pkill -f ollama && sleep 3`
53	**⚠ NEVER benchmark multiple models in sequence** — full sweep freezes M2 Pro 16GB. Test one model, read result, decide next.
54	
55	Monitor load before spawning: `./Scripts/offload.sh --list`
56	
57	## Claude Code Subagent Pattern
58	
59	When delegating via Agent tool:
60	```
61	Agent(
62	  description: "<3-5 word task>",

64	  prompt: "Caveman terse. [role]. [task]. [files]. [output format].",
65	  run_in_background: true  // for fire-and-forget work
66	)
67	```
68	
69	Swarm = multiple parallel Agent calls in one message.
70	Max parallel: 8–14 (memory-bound, not Agent-bound).
71	Main thread: overseer, router, and final merge only.
72	
73	## Offload CLI (direct shell)

75	```bash
76	# Single model
77	./Scripts/ai @deepseek "analyze this function for edge cases"
78	./Scripts/ai @qwen "summarize these notes"

11	
12	# Compact Optimizer
13	
14	One job: build the smallest possible hint that tells /compact exactly what must survive.
15	
16	## Research Grounding
17	
18	| Paper | Core Rule |
19	|-------|-----------|
20	| Selective Context (EMNLP 2023) | Drop what is reconstructable from general knowledge. Preserve what is unique to this session. |
21	| LLMLingua (EMNLP 2023) | Compress reasoning/exploration 60–80%. Compress instructions/constraints ≤20%. |
22	| H2O MIT (NeurIPS 2023) | Always retain the last user correction + last known file state — they are attention sinks. |
23	
24	---
25	
26	## Survival Priority Hierarchy
27	
28	Rank 1 — **Never drop** (session-unique, irreplaceable):
29	- Active branch name and working directory
30	- Files modified in this session (paths + what changed)
31	- User corrections, explicit rejections, aversion decisions
32	- Definition of done / success criteria
33	- Last error message or test failure state
34	- Approved plan steps and which are complete
35	
36	Rank 2 — **Compress heavily** (preserve meaning, strip words):
37	- Current task description (1 sentence max)
38	- Key constraints stated by user
39	- Architecture decisions made
40	
41	Rank 3 — **Drop entirely** (reconstructable, low self-information):
42	- Exploration text ("let me look at...", "I'll check...")
43	- Preambles and acknowledgments
44	- Reasoning narration that led to a decision already made
45	- Redundant tool call descriptions (keep results, drop scaffolding)
46	- Any content the model could reproduce from the codebase alone
47	
48	---
49	
50	## Compact Hint Template
51	
52	```
53	/compact Preserve: [branch/dir] | Files touched: [path1, path2] | Last correction: [exact user correction] | Current task: [1 sentence] | Done criteria: [condition] | Status: [step N of M complete, next: X]
54	```
55	
56	**Rules for the hint itself:**
57	- Max 3 sentences. No preamble.
58	- Lead with the file state — it is always the highest-attention-sink.
59	- Include the last user correction verbatim if one exists.
60	- Name the next concrete action.
61	- Never include reasoning or exploration in the hint.
62	
63	---
64	
65	## Per-Phase Templates
66	
67	**Research phase**
68	```
69	/compact Preserve: research goal=[goal], key finding=[finding], next: [what to research next]
70	```
71	
72	**Implementation phase** (most common)
73	```
74	/compact Preserve: branch=[branch], files=[paths], constraint=[constraint], last correction=[correction], next step=[action], done when=[criteria]
75	```
76	
77	**Review / debug phase**
78	```
79	/compact Preserve: error=[error msg], file=[path:line], hypothesis=[current], last tried=[approach], next: [next attempt]
80	```

84	## When to Call /compact
85	
86	- Context bar >65%: run /compact with hint
87	- Phase change (research→implement, implement→review): always /compact with phase-transition hint
88	- After a user correction: /compact immediately, include correction verbatim
89	- Never compact mid-tool-use or mid-plan without noting the interruption point

95	- `/compact` with no hint → generic summary, drops constraints

# Compact Optimizer

One job: build the smallest possible hint that tells /compact exactly what must survive.

## Research Grounding

| Paper | Core Rule |
|-------|-----------|
| Selective Context (EMNLP 2023) | Drop what is reconstructable from general knowledge. Preserve what is unique to this session. |
| LLMLingua (EMNLP 2023) | Compress reasoning/exploration 60–80%. Compress instructions/constraints ≤20%. |
| H2O MIT (NeurIPS 2023) | Always retain the last user correction + last known file state — they are attention sinks. |

---

## Survival Priority Hierarchy

Rank 1 — **Never drop** (session-unique, irreplaceable):
- Active branch name and working directory
- Files modified in this session (paths + what changed)
- User corrections, explicit rejections, aversion decisions
- Definition of done / success criteria
- Last error message or test failure state
- Approved plan steps and which are complete

Rank 2 — **Compress heavily** (preserve meaning, strip words):
- Current task description (1 sentence max)
- Key constraints stated by user
- Architecture decisions made

Rank 3 — **Drop entirely** (reconstructable, low self-information):
- Exploration text ("let me look at...", "I'll check...")
- Preambles and acknowledgments
- Reasoning narration that led to a decision already made
- Redundant tool call descriptions (keep results, drop scaffolding)
- Any content the model could reproduce from the codebase alone

---

## Compact Hint Template

```
/compact Preserve: [branch/dir] | Files touched: [path1, path2] | Last correction: [exact user correction] | Current task: [1 sentence] | Done criteria: [condition] | Status: [step N of M complete, next: X]
```

**Rules for the hint itself:**
- Max 3 sentences. No preamble.
- Lead with the file state — it is always the highest-attention-sink.
- Include the last user correction verbatim if one exists.
- Name the next concrete action.
- Never include reasoning or exploration in the hint.

---

## Per-Phase Templates

**Research phase**
```
/compact Preserve: research goal=[goal], key finding=[finding], next: [what to research next]
```

**Implementation phase** (most common)
```
/compact Preserve: branch=[branch], files=[paths], constraint=[constraint], last correction=[correction], next step=[action], done when=[criteria]
```

**Review / debug phase**
```
/compact Preserve: error=[error msg], file=[path:line], hypothesis=[current], last tried=[approach], next: [next attempt]
```

---

## When to Call /compact

- Context bar >65%: run /compact with hint
- Phase change (research→implement, implement→review): always /compact with phase-transition hint
- After a user correction: /compact immediately, include correction verbatim
- Never compact mid-tool-use or mid-plan without noting the interruption point

---

## Anti-patterns (never do these)

- `/compact` with no hint → generic summary, drops constraints
- Hint longer than 3 sentences → defeats compression purpose
- Including reasoning in the hint → low self-information, wastes hint budget
- Compacting after a failed approach without writing an Aversion Memory node first

---

## Aversion Memory Gate

Per the NUDIMMUD Aversion Memory Protocol: if you are compacting after a **failed branch**, first write the failure reason to an Aversion Memory node, THEN compact. The compact hint should reference the aversion: `last aversion: [reason]`.
